title: Can a G1 humanoid nail a 4x8 sheet lying flat on a table?
summary: MuJoCo whole-body statics of the Menagerie Unitree G1 pushing a 3.4 kg nailer straight down with its feet planted (reach 0.2–0.8 m, sideways 0–0.8 m, hand height 0.4–1.4 m, pushes of 0, 50 and 100 N, torque and friction limits). A table does not help: at 50 N only 30 of 693 cells are held (94 with no push, none at 100 N), limited by the waist and wrist pitch motors and by the solver’s balance rule. The best plan, with the table top 1.0–1.1 m high and the feet 0.25 m from the edge, reaches 48 of the sheet’s 62 nails in 16 stances, worse than the 13 stances for all 62 on a wall (buildbot-stance); those nails take 43–54 s plus 15 re-stances, equal to the 372 s hand estimate at 23–24 s per re-stance. The push to seat a nail, nailer length, table standoff and re-stance time are swept, not sourced; the IK stays near the home pose with the centre of mass over the feet, so this is an upper bound on difficulty; no collisions, walking or recoil.
lede: can a G1 humanoid nail a 4x8 sheet lying flat on a table? Not better than on a wall: pushing down at 50 N with its feet planted it holds only 30 of 693 reach cells, reaching 48 of the sheet's 62 nails in 16 stances (13 stances for all 62 on a wall), and matching hand nailing (372 s) only if each re-stance takes under 23-24 s (push, standoff and re-stance time are swept, not sourced; static IK, no walking).
